subject: Atrium Finance — unexpected throughput + p99 spike after q8 rollout (CTO handoff)
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@atriumfinance.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>; ops+alerts@atriumfinance.com
Cc: Tom Hughes <thughes@atriumfinance.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T13:12:00-04:00
Subject: Sudden throughput collapse / 5xx spike after v5.2 + q8 rollout

Hannah —

We just saw a major degradation after the v5.2 with q8 rollout this morning (started ~12:45 ET). Our production throughput dropped ~35% and p99 latency jumped from ~420ms to >2.2s for our long-context flows. We're also seeing a 4.2% 5xx rate on user-facing endpoints (previously under 0.1%). This is impacting live transactions.

I attached a small sample of failing requests and timestamps (sample-failing-requests.csv). We rolled no changes on our side. Can your team confirm if the q8 rollout included any kernel changes or cache settings that could cause this? CTO Elena Soto is looped in and is asking for a firm mitigation plan and ETA.

Elena Soto
CTO, Atrium Finance
(elena.soto@atriumfinance.com)

Attachments: sample-failing-requests.csv

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@atriumfinance.com>, ops+alerts@atriumfinance.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T13:25:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse / 5xx spike after v5.2 + q8 rollout

Thanks Elena — really sorry about this. We're on it.

Immediate plan (next 2 hours):
- Triage: Rishi is pulling perf traces and kernel logs now.
- Mitigate: propose a traffic split to route 80% to the previous float model and 20% to q8 to reduce exposure while we investigate.
- Call: can we do a quick sync at 14:00 ET? I will invite our SRE/EE leads.

Please expect an update within 30–45 minutes. We'll include an explicit rollback timeline if we can't find a targeted mitigation.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
Tel: +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@atriumfinance.com>, ops+alerts@atriumfinance.com
Date: 2026-05-21T14:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse / 5xx spike after v5.2 + q8 rollout — initial findings

On Thu, May 21, 2026 at 13:12 Elena Soto <elena.soto@atriumfinance.com> wrote:
> Hannah —
> We just saw a major degradation after the v5.2 with q8 rollout this morning...

Quick update from infra: we ingested the perf logs and sample traces. Key signals:
- q8 kernel path is causing increased KV cache churn on long-context sessions (requests with >6k tokens). Cache eviction rates spike and that induces synchronous cache population calls which block the fast path.
- Memory pressure on some infer nodes triggers a fallback to a CPU-assisted code path for a subset of shards; that path adds ~1.6s to p99.
- Error modes are primarily timeouts and a small class of OOM-related 5xx from one pool (pool-17).

Attachments: perf-log-2026-05-21.tar.gz (perf counters, kernel traces), I included a short failure trace.

Recommendation: immediate traffic split 80/20 to previous float model + increase warm cache reservations for long-context sessions. If traffic split isn't feasible quickly, we should schedule a full rollback of q8 for Atrium (safe and fast).

I'll start instrumentation to verify the split effects; preliminary ETA for that measurement: ~25 minutes.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SWE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T15:05:00-04:00
Subject: Internal: Atrium escalation — ask for rollback authorization + credit proposal

Team —

Summary: Atrium production saw a throughput drop (~35%), p99 jump (~420ms -> >2.2s), and elevated 5xx after the v5.2 + q8 rollout. Rishi's analysis points to KV cache thrash + memory-pressure fallbacks on the q8 runtime for long-context flows. Current external ask: CTO wants an ETA and a concrete mitigation.

Proposed immediate actions (need approvals):
1) Authorize a full rollback of q8 for Atrium to the previous float model (safe code path, rollback window: 20 minutes). This is the fastest customer-visible mitigation.
2) Offer Atrium a service credit of 10% for the impacted hour and an engineering postmortem with timeline.
3) Schedule a joint incident retrofit with their SREs to tune warm-cache reservations and verify q8 kernel patches before re-rolling.

Approve rollback and credit? If yes, I'll coordinate the rollback and draft the customer message. We should also consider pausing any further q8 rollouts to high long-context customers until the cache eviction fix is in.

Hannah

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@atriumfinance.com>, Tom Hughes <thughes@atriumfinance.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T18:45:00-04:00
Subject: Atrium update: rollback scheduled (19:10 UTC) and next steps

Elena / Tom —

Thank you for your patience. We will perform a rollback of the q8 rollout for Atrium at 19:10 UTC (confirmed window 19:10–19:30 UTC). Expected customer impact during the rollback: brief routing stabilization (~1–2 minutes) while we shift traffic back to the previous float model; p99 should return to baseline within 10 minutes of rollback completion.

Immediate items delivered:
- We have flagged and isolated pool-17; Rishi's team is increasing warm-cache reservations for long-context sessions and adding defensive timeouts.
- We created OPS ticket OPS-927 and a runbook for the rollback step (attached runbook PDF).
- We will provide a postmortem within 48 hours and a 10% credit for the impacted hour.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll send a short status update after rollback completes.

— Hannah
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-runbook-v2.pdf, OPS-927 link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-927
